draft: We held that God does not compel the soul, and that the soul has real power to turn toward him or away [[alx.term.autexousia]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Formation worked through the soul's own turning, never around it [[alx.term.autexousia]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Origen's rule was plain: what the apostles delivered plainly is fixed, and everything else is open ground [[alx.dw.doubt]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Whether Origen held that all things will be restored, as settled doctrine, is contested [[alx.contested.origen-positions]] [[as:paraphrase]]. sentences.sentence: Whether Origen held that all things will be restored, as settled doctrine, is contested.

Clement wrote in Stromateis I.5: “Perhaps, too, philosophy was given to the Greeks directly and in the first place, until the Lord should call the Greeks. For philosophy was a guardian to bring the Greek mind to Christ, as the law was for the Hebrews. So philosophy was a preparation. It paved the way for the one who is made perfect in Christ.”
